title: How visitors move through a marketing funnel
purpose: See where a funnel loses people and why the stage conversion rate matters more than the visitor count.
sequence_reason: A funnel is a sequence of dependent stages; each stage only receives the people that the stage before it kept.
summary: Ten thousand visitors reach a landing page. Two thousand sign up, six hundred activate, and one hundred and fifty buy. The largest drop is between visit and sign-up.
explanation: Each stage keeps a share of the stage before it. Fixing the stage with the largest relative drop usually gives the largest gain.

learning_check.question: If the sign-up rate doubles and every later rate stays the same, how many buyers do you get?
learning_check.answer: Three hundred, because every later stage receives twice as many people.

scenes.heading: Four stages, one customer journey
scenes.narration: A funnel follows people from the first visit to the first purchase.

scenes.heading: The stages in order
scenes.narration: A visitor lands on the page, signs up, activates the product, and then buys. Each stage depends on the one before it.

scenes.heading: Where people drop out
scenes.narration: Ten thousand visit, two thousand sign up, six hundred activate, and one hundred fifty buy. The biggest drop is at sign up.

scenes.heading: Rates, not counts
scenes.narration: Compare stage rates. Sign up keeps twenty percent, activate thirty percent, and buy twenty five percent.
